html:
The Panama Canal is an 82 km waterway across the Isthmus of Panama that links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. The United States built it between 1904 and 1914, sparing ships the long and dangerous voyage around the tip of South America.

The isthmus had long been a crossing point. Spanish mule trains carried silver from Peru across it, and in the 1850s the Panama Railroad carried people to the California Gold Rush. In the 1880s a French company led by Ferdinand de Lesseps, builder of the Suez Canal, tried to dig a sea-level canal. It failed, beaten by landslides, money troubles and disease; more than 20,000 workers died, mostly of malaria and yellow fever.

The United States took over the project. When Colombia, which then ruled Panama, refused its terms, the US backed Panama's independence in 1903 and got control of a Canal Zone. The new plan used locks instead of a sea-level cut: ships are lifted 26 metres to Gatun Lake, made by damming the Chagres River, and lowered again on the other side. Army doctor William Gorgas brought disease under control by attacking the mosquitoes that carried it. Most of the work was done by labourers from the Caribbean, above all Barbados.

The canal opened in August 1914, days after the First World War began. It shortened the sea route from New York to San Francisco by about 13,000 km. Control passed to Panama on 31 December 1999. It was widened for larger ships in 2016 (see Panama Canal expansion).
sum: The Panama Canal is an 82 km waterway across the Isthmus of Panama that links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. The United States built it between 1904 and 1914, sparing ships the long and dangerous voyage around the tip of South America.
